authority_note.forge_removal: Owner decision 2026-10-13: Forge is removed from the Lab. XMage is the single rules engine; there is no secondary_engine. Sealed epochs and signed records that name Forge keep their original identities as history and are never rewritten.

current_runtime.launch: the XMage bridge started with the single argument full-game (org.commanderlab.xmage.Main full-game); any other argument shape starts the B4-D compatibility bridge, which is no longer the production runtime

historical_phase85.note: Preserved only for Phase 8.5 provenance; not current provider truth.

primary_engine.role: real pinned XMage Production Provider on the full-game lane (Owner-signed Freeze 2026-10-10, D5 runtime switch): 2..6-player Commander Free-for-All with external out-of-process pilots, decision-scoped complete legal actions and submission per declared decision class, public event-log export, semantic replay export with clean-process verification, per-game shutdown; one game per JVM process. The B4-D compatibility bridge stays available for its historical surfaces only and is not the production runtime.

truth_boundary: B4-D is external_rules_engine evidence for real pinned XMage deck import, Commander construction/start, live state observation, current-priority decision/legal-action handoff, real priority passing, stale decision/action rejection, bounded submission-ready targetless/nonmodal action execution including a real Rograkh commander cast, an externally exportable monotonic bridge audit event stream with action/decision identity and pre/post state hashes, and explicit per-game XMage lifecycle cleanup/reuse. The audit stream covers real bridge/XMage lifecycle and externally controlled action boundaries; it is not claimed to be an exhaustive raw internal XMage GameEvent tap. Globally complete legal-action enumeration and action submission remain unproven because target, mode, choice and combat classes are incomplete. Mulligan, seed-control, replay and complete production game-loop coverage remain unproven. This is not win-rate evidence and does not make XMage a production-ready provider.

architecture_freeze.note: selected_provider is the architecture-level selection made at the Freeze. The D5 runtime switch moved the launched runtime (production_bridge) to the full-game lane; provider_decision, current_runtime and primary_engine.production_ready record that switch. D17 stays a bounded limitation: pilots out of process, no third-party code in the engine JVM; stronger isolation is a gate before any untrusted pilot.
